name: com.midmanstudio.questly
description: Game-agnostic quest engine on top of the DixScript (.mdix) database: declarative objectives/prereqs/rewards, an automatic unlock watcher plus manual override, push-based progress reporting, and a pluggable evaluator hook for game-specific objective/prereq types. Zero game-specific logic — a consuming game layers its own interpretation on top, the same relationship it has with com.midmanstudio.alembic. Still deliberately headless: no UI, no dialogue/proximity triggers, no missions-tab rendering -- a diegetic GTA-style quest-giver flow needs no package changes at all (AVAILABLE state + the existing StartQuest() convenience method already are 'accept'; not calling it is 'reject'; a host's own trigger script calling it directly is 'auto-accept on arrival'). Reward-claim tracking (IsRewardClaimed/CanClaimReward/TryClaimReward/AllRewardsClaimed/GetNextClaimableReward, a RewardClaimed event, and claim rows in the hybrid persistence model) supports a COD-style missions-tab where completing a quest and collecting its reward(s) are two separate, UI-driven steps -- claim order follows a quest's existing Rewards list order. Native time scheduling adds an optional per-quest ScheduleDefinition (ONE_SHOT or RECURRING) driven by a single AdvanceTime(double now) clock pump, where 'now' is an opaque host-fed number with no assumed epoch or unit -- real seconds, an abstract day-counter, whatever the host's clock actually is. Covers three shapes without any new persistence model: a limited-time event that goes permanently EXPIRED (new QuestState value) if its window closes unmet; a main-path quest that keeps reappearing every cycle until completed once, then stops for good (StopAfterFirstCompletion); and a capped login-streak/daily-checkin track (StopAfterFirstCompletion = false) where each cycle unlocks the next reward in list order via a new, separate per-cycle claim API (CanClaimCycleReward/TryClaimCycleReward) gated on a monotonic CyclesCompleted counter rather than live QuestState -- so a reward earned on a missed day never expires, it just sits there claimable whenever the player comes back. An attempt already ACTIVE is never cut off by a closing window regardless of schedule kind; objectives reset fresh at the start of each new RECURRING cycle.
